title: Inverse image of sheaves of sets preserves colimits and finite products
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces, and for a sheaf of sets $\mathcal G$ on $Y$ let $f^{-1}\mathcal G$ be its inverse image, the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf $f_p\mathcal G:U\mapsto\varinjlim_{V\supseteq f(U)}\mathcal G(V)$ (colimit of sets [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]), functorial in $\mathcal G$, as in [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] (2), (3) with values in sets. Then: (a) $f^{-1}$ is left adjoint to the direct image $f_*$ (sheaves of sets on $X$ to sheaves of sets on $Y$, $f_*\mathcal F(V)=\mathcal F(f^{-1}V)$), hence for every small category $I$ and every diagram $(\mathcal G_i)_{i\in I}$ of sheaves of sets on $Y$ with colimit $(\mathcal G,(c_i:\mathcal G_i\to\mathcal G)_i)$ in the category of sheaves of sets on $Y$, $(f^{-1}\mathcal G,(f^{-1}c_i)_i)$ is a colimit of $(f^{-1}\mathcal G_i)_i$ in the category of sheaves of sets on $X$; (b) $f^{-1}$ commutes with finite limits; in particular for sheaves of sets $\mathcal G_1,\dots,\mathcal G_n$ on $Y$ ($n\ge0$) with product $\mathcal P=\prod_k\mathcal G_k$ (computed sectionwise, $\mathcal P(V)=\prod_k\mathcal G_k(V)$, projections $p_k$), the morphism $f^{-1}\mathcal P\to\prod_kf^{-1}\mathcal G_k$ with components $f^{-1}p_k$ is an isomorphism (for $n=0$: $f^{-1}$ of the final sheaf is final).

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma (Tag 008K, label lemma-f-map: $f^{-1}$ is left adjoint to $f_*$) with Categories, Lemma (Tag 0038, lemma-adjoint-exact) for (a); for (b), Sheaves, Lemma (Tag 008H, lemma-stalk-pullback: stalks of $f^{-1}\mathcal G$ are stalks of $\mathcal G$) together with Categories, Lemma 002W (lemma-directed-commutes: directed colimits commute with finite limits), so the comparison map is bijective on stalks; used in literature/stacks-project/etale-cohomology.tex, proof of Lemma 59.82.1 (Tag 09ZG, line 15125: restriction to $Z$ is a left adjoint)
